quote.author: XFreeze
quote.name: X Freeze
quote.text:
Since I posted about using Grok Bot to buy things with my credit card, so many people have been asking whether it’s actually safe

What’s actually strange to me is that for decades, people have been handing their credit cards to complete strangers at restaurants. Someone takes your card, walks away with it, swipes it through a machine, processes your payment, and brings it back

And most people don’t even think twice about it

We live in a digital world where software already handles enormous amounts of financial transactions every single day

Tbh these days is actually more safer to let AI/SI do the shopping for you then you doing the shopping for you

with AI/SI agents, you can sandbox them, give them limited permissions, and have them ask for your approval before making important decisions…. These days the latest models are really good at understanding the real world and they’re extremely cautious about the things that they do for you

From what I’ve personally experienced with Grok Bot, it’s actually extraordinary how cautious it is when handling these tasks

If something is expensive or really needs your attention, it simply pauses for a moment and asks you what you want to do. It gives you a few simple options, you choose what you want, and the final decision is still yours where you have to make

And all of this happens without you having to go through the entire hassle of shopping yourself

I’ve personally watched how carefully Grok Bot handles these things, and I’m really impressed by it

Even Elon said that if Grok Bot makes a mistake with your purchase, they’ll make you whole

That tells you how much confidence the team has in what they have built…. and it is really amazing. I just run out of limits every single week because I’ve been using it so much

The interesting part is
Grok Bot actually does a better job shopping than you in many situations

Think about how often you open shopping website to buy something, see some random banner or attractive advertisement, and suddenly you’re looking at three other things you never even needed 😂

This happens all the time with online shopping

These websites are absolutely filled with advertisements designed to grab your attention and get you to buy more things

But Grok Bot can actually research what you need, compare products, find better deals, and save you a lot of money instead of getting you distracted in that entire mess of advertising

And the amount of time it saves is actually just ridiculous

You don’t have to spend hours browsing different websites, comparing prices, going through endless product listings, filling out forms, and handling every single step of the purchase

You just tell your Grok Bot what you want, and it handles so much of the work for you. And whenever something actually needs your attention, it simply asks

It gets so much easier, and once you start using these Grok Bot for everyday tasks, you really begin to understand how incredibly useful it really is

posts.text:
HOW ELON MUSK AND HIS BROTHER'S FIRST VACATION ALMOST TURNED INTO A TRAGEDY... AND HOW IS IT CONNECTED TO THE SUCCESS OF SPACEX?

december 2000. Elon has just been pushed out as CEO of PayPal. he's 29, rich on paper, and for once he takes a break

he flies to South Africa with his brother Kimbal. the bush, a safari, the place they grew up running around in

Kimbal laughs about it now:
"we'd go to the bush all the time. i don't think we ever took malaria tablets"

this time they did. it didn't matter

january 2001. Elon is back in California and something is badly wrong. doctors check for malaria. negative

Kimbal: "i couldn't figure out what was wrong with him"

then their uncle, a doctor in South Africa, says it straight: "he has malaria. check again"

he was right. malaria hides in the body. and this was the deadly kind

Elon: "i had a severe case of malaria. almost died"
"i lost like 50 pounds"
"took me over six months to get back to normal"

and his lesson from all of it:
"no more vacations"

now the part that matters

six months of recovery. no company to run. a guy who almost died at 29 starts asking one question: what do i do next?

he checks NASA's website to see when humans are going to Mars. there's no plan. nothing

so he flies to Moscow. to buy ICBMs. "literally"
"i can afford to pay under nine million dollars for an ICBM. but not 20"

the Russians keep raising the price. he walks out

and instead of looking for a cheaper seller, he asks a different question: why are rockets so expensive in the first place? the metal, the fuel, the parts cost a small slice of the price tag. the rest is how the industry builds them

so instead of buying a rocket, he decides to build one

napkin math:
the rocket he was willing to pay for: under $9M
where the Russians were pushing: $20M+
his cut from the PayPal sale to eBay in 2002: ~$180M
how much of it went into SpaceX: ~$100M
SpaceX today: valued at $800B+

the company is now worth ~8,000x the money he put in

the first three Falcon 1 launches failed. the fourth reached orbit in 2008. he's said there was money for basically one more try

most people come back from almost dying and slow down. Elon came back and bet more than half of everything on the most expensive thing on earth

a vacation almost killed him. the comeback built SpaceX

When @Starlink helped rescue four sailors and three dogs. ♥️

Four people and three dogs were stranded after a storm badly damaged their boat in the South Pacific. They were more than 300 km from New Caledonia.

They had no radio contact. They sent their location through Starlink.

A cruise ship changed course and travelled five hours to reach them. All four people and all three dogs were rescued.

This is why Starlink matters. When people need help, a working connection can save lives. This life-saving technology should be available in every part of the world.

quote.author: jukan05
quote.name: Jukan
quote.text:
This is a really interesting chart.
I attended the TrendForce San Francisco roadshow yesterday, and this chart got me thinking about a lot of things.

China is now expected to localize more than half, or close to half, of most equipment categories, excluding lithography and track.
What does this mean? It means China can now expand mature node capacity far more easily than before, using equipment made domestically within China.

Mature node foundries are booming right now, right? That's thanks to the AI supercycle driving demand for PMICs, power semiconductors, and so on.

Samsung and TSMC shutting down their mature node capacity has also helped a lot.
But here's what I imagine... that China could oversupply mature foundry capacity.

Think about it. If China can be self sufficient in equipment, there's no limit to how far it can expand capacity. Then are companies like TI, with large revenue exposure to China, really safe?

I think it's time to take another look at Western mature foundry companies with a high share of China revenue.

Of course, I'm not saying sell TI right now. I'm just saying we should think about whether it makes sense to hold them for 10 years or more, like Coca Cola.

If you have a different view, please feel free to share it. I’d love to learn.

posts.text: Grok @Bot can call restaurants by phone and book you a table

quote.author: BrianRoemmele
quote.name: Brian Roemmele
quote.text:
“HUNNY MY GROK BOT CALLED OUR FAVORITE ITALIAN RESTAURANT AND MADE US RESERVATIONS”

I built a Grok Bot whose only job is to pick up the phone and book you a table at restaurant. Literally make the call in a beautiful Grok voice. It is absolutely amazing! And it’s free.

Try it: https://x.ai/bot/TIMrxLJHbEEpdr25yYgvL

Yesterday I told it "book Gourmet Italia in Temecula, 4 people, tonight, around 7." It found the restaurant's number on its own, asked how flexible we were on time, what name to book under, and what callback number to give. Then it read everything back and waited for my OK before it dialed. One call covers every time that works for us, so there's no back and forth.

When the call ends, it tells me what happened in plain English, quotes what the restaurant actually said, and offers to put the reservation on my calendar. If I don't have a calendar connected, it hands me a file that opens right in Apple Calendar.

 A Proposal: Grok Phone

Grok Bot needs its own phone number to make and receive calls. I connected a calling service called ClawCall, and the free tier gave me 30 calls or 30 minutes to start. I have no connection to that company. It's just what I used. Once Grok Bot has a number, it stops being something you type to and becomes something that can actually get things done in the real world. @Grok you need an old tyme phone service, buddy.

I built some guardrails. It never hands over a credit card or deposit info, never leaves voicemails unless you ask, makes one call at a time, and never calls on its own.

And this isn't really about restaurants. Change a few words and the same bot can:

- Book a haircut, a massage, or a dentist cleaning

- Get a tee time or a court reservation

- Check if a hotel has a room or will let you check in early

- Schedule a car service or an oil change

- Call around for quotes from a plumber, an electrician, or a caterer

This is one of many ways I use Grok Bot to build businesses and make life easier. The calls I used to put off for days now take me 30 seconds.

I made it shareable, so you can grab "Call A Restaurant Reservation" and use it yourself.

LINK: https://x.ai/bot/TIMrxLJHbEEpdr25yYgvL
